previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Meléndez, a man with chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and a history of heavy alcohol use, was admitted with acute right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. His symptoms were attributed to alcoholic hepatitis and gastritis/duodenitis, with no evidence of gallbladder disease or pancreatitis. Liver enzymes and bilirubin were elevated on admission but improved during the hospital stay. Hypokalemia was corrected, and he was monitored for alcohol withdrawal without complications. His chest pain was consistent with stable angina, ruled out for acute cardiac injury. He was restarted on losartan for hypertension, educated on medication adherence, and discharged home with plans for shelter support and outpatient follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
Hospital course by problem:

# Alcohol intoxication/withdrawal: Ethanol level of 379 on 
admission. He received thiamine and folate in the ED. Patient 
placed on CIWA, scoring in ___ on day of admission. By HD2, he 
was scoring ___ and therefore taken off CIWA with ativan PRN for 
anxiety. He continued on daily thiamine, folate, and MVI. He was 
monitored daily for signs of withrawal, but remained stable.    

# RUQ pain: AST:ALT ~ 2:1 on admission consistent with 
alcohol-induced liver injury, bilirubin level normal. Alcoholic 
hepatitis with capsule irritation was considered for diagnosis. 
Other possiblities included PUD especially given reports of 
hematemesis. The patient received an RUQ US which was 
unremarkable for cholecystitis, cholangitis, choledocolithiasis, 
cholelithiasis. The patient remained afebrile with a normal WBC 
throughout his hospital stay. Likewise, CT abdomen with no 
notable findings. GI recommnedations after consult included 
lidocaine path for R rib pain, max dose PPI for likely alcoholic 
gastritis, and no need for EGD on this admission. The patient 
was managed on max dose PPI and lidocaine patch with improvement 
in RUQ pain.

#N/V: Patient developed nausea and vomiting during hospital 
stay. Some report of related dizziness, but mostly N/V was after 
each meal. Non-bilious, non-bloody emesis (guiac negative). 
Patient was managed on zofran as needed with resolution of N/V 
by discharge. Of note, patient was observed placing soup in his 
emesis basin. pH of liquid in emesis basin was higher than 
gastric contents in someone on high dose PPI. Patient's alleged 
vomiting resolved once basins were taken out of his room and he 
came to terms with his discharge status.

# Paroxysmal Afib/Aflutter: Long history of afib/flutter. CHADS2 
score 2. Currently NSR. Anticoagulation regimen unclear on 
admission (recently switched bewteen lovenox and dabigatran). We 
contacted his cardiologist, who said he has no preference for 
lovenox vs dabigatran. Patient was started on lovenox 80 SC Q12H 
after guiac of emesis was negative. The patient was started on 
metoprolol 12.5mg BID given his heart history and long term 
benefit, which was well tolerated given borderline high BP and 
HR in ___. He continued his home ASA 81.

# Hypertension: continued Losartan, started metoprolol as above.
